test_title: PYST 17: SSC JE CE - Reasoning (Held on: 23 Mar 2021 Shift 1)
subject: reasoning
question:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions based on those statements. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

**Statements:**

All the snakes are cats.

All the cats are frogs.

Some monkeys are frogs.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some frogs are snakes

II. Some monkeys are cats

III. All the cats are snakes

options.text: Only conclusion I and III follows
Only conclusion I and II follows

solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as below,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/163aab916225b39e8167d804008d8ec59ecdb5d79bc66224c845158af397efb6.png] 

Conclusions:

1. Some frogs are snakes → True (It is clear from the given statement that all the snakes are frogs that means some frogs also be snakes will be true).

2. Some monkeys are cat → False (It is clear that some frogs are monkeys and vice versa but there is no direct relation given between monkeys and cats so we can't surely comment anything about this).

3. All cats are snakes → False (It is clear that all snakes are cats but we can't say that all the cats are snakes because no direct relation given from the cat side).

Thus, **Only conclusions I follow.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__**

Suppose for an Example:** All A are B.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c43cff4f70c5d472ce3fe18b9c506bab8f57970d146297eb5eca90b87231ef0c.png] 

If we go from **In to Out** means from A to B then **cases with All and some will be true like All A are B and Some A are B**.

But if we go **Out to In** then only cases with **Some will be true** and **All will be can't say like Some B are A will be true but All B are A will be can't say.**
